SINK: Explicit 409 'Email is already registered' (existing email) vs 409 'Organization already exists; ask an admin for an invite' (new email + existing domain) vs 201 Created (new email + new domain). An attacker can probe emails and domain names to confirm which accounts/organizations exist without authentication.

extra.message: Unbounded memory consumption in CSV ticket export

metadata.proof: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: Any authenticated user hitting GET /api/tickets/export.csv. SINK: .all() loads every matching Ticket row plus eagerly-loaded relationships (organization, requester, category) into memory. A customer_user with many tickets or a support_admin triggers loading the entire table into memory. No limit, offset, or streaming iterator is applied.

extra.message: Unbounded admin report export rows cause memory exhaustion

metadata.proof: Admin CSV report export uses .all() with no row limit, buffering every ticket in the database into memory. scoped_report_query for support_admin returns ALL tickets unfiltered. This creates a straightforward DoS vector.

extra.message: API keys never expire

metadata.proof: The ApiKey model has is_active, last_used_at, and created_at but no expires_at or max-age field. Keys created via /api/admin/api-keys remain valid indefinitely unless manually revoked, violating least-privilege and increasing blast radius if a key is leaked.

extra.message: API keys remain valid after creator account is disabled

metadata.proof: api_key_auth validates only that the ApiKey row is active; it never checks whether key.created_by.is_active is still True (compare current_user() at deps.py:33-34 which checks user.is_active). Disabling or offboarding a user does not revoke their integration keys, allowing disabled users to keep acting through the API via /api/integrations/ endpoints.
